correctness.rationale: Headline: Lemma (every rank-exactly-3 matroid has connected ordered compatible-pair exchange graphs of diameter <=3) + spectrum D3=0,D4=1,D5=2,D6=D7=D8=3 (D*=3) + extremal witnesses + m<=6 per-type table. Verified: (1) Restriction argument sound: for compatible P,Q with support T (|T|<=6), M|T has rank 3 and pair-graph is identical to that in M, so [6] check lifts. (2) Finite half replayed: inputs/artifacts/lemma_check.py ran 6.8s, 2053 nonempty rank-3 families (empty excluded), all connected, max diameter 3, 901 attaining 3; exchange filter and BFS adjacency (no-op excluded, multiset class) correctly implement definitions. (3) m<=6 census independently recomputed: line-family backtracking with S_m canonical dedup gives types 1,2,4,9 and labeled counts 1/5/31/352 (excluding degenerate empty-basis family; raw enumeration gives 2/6/32/353 including it); every line family satisfies exchange axiom (0 failures); diameter distributions {0:1},{1:2},{2:4},{3:8,2:1} give claimed D3..D6. (4) All census witness endpoints are bases, compatible, BFS distance equals claimed diameter and stored path length equals diameter with every step a valid symmetric exchange. (5) U(3,7)/U(3,8) disjoint-swap pair BFS distance 3 confirmed; 1-element-per-step lower bound and explicit 3-step path sound; Fano pair ((012),(345))->((345),(012)) confirmed bases with BFS distance 3 and valid 3-step path. Ordered-pair, compatibility, and boundary D3=0 handled correctly. Computer-assisted parts are exact stdlib bitmask/BFS, replayable.

originality.rationale: Nearest priors checked live: Yu-Yuen arXiv:2510.04163 proves White connectivity for paving matroids (covers simple rank-3) with no distances; Berczi-Schwarcz arXiv:2203.01779 proves min{r,r-|A1 cap B1|+1} bound and polynomial shortest-sequence algorithm for split matroids (rank-3 implies <=3) with K4 tightness example, but no per-type/per-order diameter spectrum, no D_m/D*, no extremal-pair census on m<=8; Berczi-Matravolgyi-Schwarcz arXiv:2311.07130 concerns regular matroids with asymptotic bound; Hanaka et al. arXiv:2409.07848 proves reachability polynomial but shortest c log n-hard to approximate, motivating benchmarks but computing none here. Exact D_m values, full m<=6 per-type table (1/2/4/9 types), and logged shortest paths are in no catalogue (which store representability/Tutte) and are not mechanically implied by a connectivity theorem, a general <=3 bound, or an algorithm alone — they require exhaustive pair-graph BFS over all types. Internal SCOPE026 overlap is Tutte T(2,0) maximization on same 68-type domain, containing no exchange distances. Lemma's extension to all (including non-split/non-simple) rank-3 matroids goes beyond the split-only bound.

value.rationale: Strongest headline (D_m spectrum 0,1,2,3,3,3 with D*=3, proved rank-3 diameter<=3 lemma, uniform + Fano distance-3 extremal witnesses with logged shortest paths, complete m<=6 per-type table) is a rigorously established exact invariant of a natural motivated object. Object/invariant motivated before computation by White's conjecture / toric quadrics / reconfiguration-optimization program where reachability is increasingly settled but shortest paths are log-hard, creating demand for exact small-scope ground truth to calibrate polynomial routing and rewriting bounds. Scope m<=8 simple rank-3 is natural (first nontrivial reconfiguration class, exhaustively enumerable, contains Fano-type symmetric configurations, matches 8-point catalogue boundary without reusing labels). Values were not known and not mechanically implied. Future White-program work can reasonably retrieve D*, D_m, extremal pairs, and paths as regression tests. Per guidance, an exact invariant of this form need not carry a new general theorem; incomplete m=7,8 type census is honestly disclosed (only D7=D8=3 claimed via Lemma plus uniform witnesses) and does not erase headline value.

checked_sources.finding: Proves White reachability for paving matroids (covers simple rank-3); connectivity only, no distances, diameters, or extremal pairs.
checked_sources.title: Yu-Yuen — White's Conjecture for Paving Matroids

checked_sources.finding: For split matroids proves exchange distance <= min{r,r-|A1 cap B1|+1} with polynomial shortest-sequence algorithm; rank-3 implies <=3 but gives no per-type/per-order spectrum, no D_m/D*, no extremal census on m<=8. K4 example shows bound tight in general, not the census.
checked_sources.title: Berczi-Schwarcz — Exchange distance of basis pairs in split matroids

checked_sources.finding: Regular-matroid basis-pair reconfiguration with first polynomial upper bound; different class, asymptotic, not rank-3 <=8 exact spectrum.
checked_sources.title: Berczi-Matravolgyi-Schwarcz — Reconfiguration of basis pairs in regular matroids

checked_sources.finding: Basis-sequence reachability polynomial but shortest transformation NP-hard to approximate within c log n; establishes demand for exact small benchmarks.
checked_sources.title: Hanaka et al. — Basis sequence reconfiguration in the union of matroids
